title: Runtime Energy-Aware Scheduling and Profiling Playbook
author: Ananya Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook documents our approach to energy- and power-aware kernel scheduling for the Redwood serving runtime, and prescribes a repeatable profiling and benchmarking workflow for validating energy-related optimizations. The goal is to reduce total energy per inference (Joules/token) while preserving latency SLOs and model-quality constraints.

Scope
-----
Applies to: the serving runtime (scheduler, kernel mapper, and dispatch layers) and the GPU-hotpath kernel implementations. Covers: telemetry, local and cluster-level scheduling policies, profiling methodology, benchmark scenarios, rollout recipes, and incident runbook steps for energy regressions. Does NOT replace thermal/firmware actions performed by cloud providers.

Motivation
----------
- Our customer demand and operational costs require optimizing energy consumption for sustained workloads (e.g., embeddings, high-QPS chat).
- Naive throughput maximization can increase energy per token due to inefficient kernel choices and poor batching alignment.
- We need a documented, repeatable way to measure energy impact of runtime changes, and safe rollout patterns that respect latency SLOs.

Goals and success criteria
-------------------------
1. Reduce median Joules/token for production embedding workloads by >=15% in targeted fleets without increasing p99 latency by >5%.
2. Establish an energy-profiling pipeline that provides reproducible per-kernel and per-request energy attribution within ±10% measurement error.
3. Add automated benchmark scenarios to CI that flag >10% regression in energy-per-token relative to baseline.

Design overview
---------------
At a high level we extend the runtime with three cooperating components:

1) Energy Estimator (lightweight):
- Runs per-device and per-kernel cost models built from microbenchmarks (see Benchmark suite section).
- Inputs: kernel name, sequence length, batch size, quantization profile, GPU model and power cap.
- Output: estimated Joules for the predicted execution path.

2) Power-Aware Scheduler Layer (policy hooks):
- Policy types: power-capped admission, energy-windowing, and cost-weighted-priority.
- Scheduler consults estimator to compute cost delta when selecting kernel variant or slotting across GPUs.
- Policies can be per-tenant, per-model, or global.

3) Telemetry & Attribution:
- Fine-grained telemetry emitted for each request: kernel sequence, execution time, energy_estimate, actual_energy_reading (when available), and decision_reason.
- Telemetry schema additions are in the Team Wiki (see Related pages).

Scheduling policies (examples)
----------------------------
- Power-capped admission: refuse or re-route requests when aggregate expected power > cluster cap threshold. Use for burst isolation on constrained fleets.
- Energy-windowing: prefer kernel variants with lower energy for long-running batched requests even at slight latency cost.
- Cost-weighted priority: score each candidate placement by (priority_score / estimated_joules) to maximize useful work per Joule.

Policy configuration table
-------------------------
Key parameter | Description | Typical value
--------------|-------------|--------------
power_cap_pct  | Percent of device sustained power that scheduler will target | 80
energy_margin  | Allowed increase in Jain-style cost to trade energy for latency | 1.10
sample_interval_s | How often to sample device power sensors for calibration | 30
window_ms      | Energy-windowing decision horizon | 2000

Profiling methodology
---------------------
Objective: capture both model-level and kernel-level energy signals with reproducible noise bounds.

1) Environment requirements:
- Isolated host or pinned node to avoid cross-tenant noise.
- Node-level power telemetry enabled (NVML/AMDuProf/etc) with sampling frequency >= 10Hz.
- Soldered measurement (external PDUs) for fleet-level validation when available.

2) Signals to collect:
- Per-request: request_id, model, kernel_variant, batch_size, seq_len, start_ts, end_ts, gpu_power_series, gpu_temp_series, inferred_joules_estimate, actual_joules_measurement (if sampling available).
- Per-device: SKU, firmware version, driver version, CUDA/cuDNN/cuFFT versions (if applicable), clock settings, power-limit.

3) Sampling strategy and noise control:
- Run each microbenchmark 50+ times and report median and 95% CI.
- For end-to-end workload runs, replay production traces with at least 10 minutes sustained windows for steady-state measurement.
- Use A/B paired tests across identical hardware to factor out ambient variation.

4) Attribution technique:
- When device-level power is coarse, perform causal attribution by: (a) collect per-kernel execution intervals; (b) integrate power trace over intervals; (c) normalize by background idle baseline measured in the same experimental window.

Benchmark suite additions
------------------------
We extend the existing perf suite with energy-focused artifacts:
- microbench-energy-generator: microbenchmarks per kernel and per-sequence-length that emit time and power traces.
- steady-state-replay: component that replays production QPS traces with controllable slotting and power caps.
- energy-ci-checker: CI task that runs selected profiles and fails on >10% energy regression.

Sample CLI commands
-------------------
# Run a microbenchmark for a kernel variant and record power
$ tools/bench/microbench-energy --model gpt-3.5-small --kernel relu-fused --batch 8 --seq 512 --iters 100 --output /tmp/bench.json

# Run steady-state replay for 10 minutes under 80% power cap
$ tools/bench/steady-replay --trace traces/embeddings_jan.bt --duration 600 --power-cap 80 --out /tmp/replay.json

Expected baseline table (example)
--------------------------------
Workload | Baseline Joules/token | Median latency (ms) | Notes
---------|-----------------------|---------------------|------
Embeddings-512b | 0.18 | 12.4 | measured on A100-80W baseline
Chat-small-64 | 0.25 | 9.2 | small model optimized with fused kernels
Rerank-32 | 0.11 | 6.8 | heavily batched workload

Runbook: Investigation for energy regression
-------------------------------------------
When CI or production telemetry shows an energy-per-token regression >10%:
1. Confirm signal: validate CI artifacts and check paired baselines.
2. Check deployment: identify which kernel variants or scheduler changes rolled out in the window (use deployment trace).
3. Perform microbench isolation: run microbench-energy for the affected kernel variants on identical hardware.
4. Collect device telemetry: driver/firmware mismatches, thermal events, power-limit changes.
5. Rollback policy: revert scheduler policy flags (feature-flag ID) and/or kernel variant to last-known-good.
6. Postmortem: populate incident in the runtime incident tracker, include root cause, mitigations, and CI guard to prevent recurrence.

Rollout and safety
------------------
- Feature gating: energy-aware scheduling is behind a server-side feature flag per datacenter region.
- Canary matrix: run in 1% of serving capacity with both telemetry sampling and P99 latency guard rails for 24 hours before broader rollout.
- Automatic fallback: if p99 latency increases by >5% or energy-per-token regresses >20% in canary, disable policy and trigger alert to oncall.

Operational considerations
------------------------
- Telemetry storage: add sampling to limit retention cost; store high-fidelity traces for windows where anomalies are detected.
- Cost accounting: update per-tenant cost buckets to include energy_adjusted_charge = baseline_unit_cost * estimated_joules / baseline_joules.
- Security: energy telemetry is internal but may include customer request identifiers; mark as internal-only and scrub PII per data management policy.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Primary owner: serving-runtime kernel and scheduler squad (oncall-channel: #runtime-kernel).
- Measurement and benchmarking steward: perf-infra team.
- Review cadence: Quarterly review of energy baselines and policy thresholds.

Related pages and artifacts
--------------------------
- Kernel mapper and scheduling policy language docs (see kernel-and-scheduling folder).
- Microbench harness repository: git:github.com/redwood-inference/bench/microbench-energy
- Team wiki: telemetry schema and event names for energy profiling.

Appendix: energy-calibration JSON example
-----------------------------------------
{
  "device_sku": "A100-80W",
  "power_limit_w": "80",
  "microbench_median_joules_per_op": "0.0042",
  "calibration_ts": "2026-02-10T18:30:00Z"
}

Appendix: quick checklist for experiments
----------------------------------------
- Reserve isolated nodes and set consistent power limits.
- Use the microbench harness to build kernel cost table.
- Run steady-state replays with paired control experiments.
- Collect at least 10 minutes steady-state windows, repeat N=5.
- Commit a benchmark artifact to the energy-bench registry before PR merge.

Notes and open questions
------------------------
- We are still validating driver/firmware contributions to per-kernel energy variance: plan to run cross-firmware experiments in Q2 2026.
- GPU vendor APIs for per-kernel energy are still imperfect; fall back to interval-based attribution when necessary.

Contact
-------
For questions, reach out to the playbook author or ping #runtime-kernel on Slack.
